chunks: 5179 - Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad narrated from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah from Abu Basir, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah عليه السلام about al-qasamah: where did it begin? He said: “It was from the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله. After the conquest of Khaybar, a man from the Ansar lagged behind his companions. They returned to search for him and found him writhing in his blood, slain. The Ansar came to the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله and said: ‘O Messenger of Allah, the Jews killed our companion.’ He said: ‘Let fifty men from among you swear that they killed him.’ They said: ‘O Messenger of Allah, shall we swear to what we did not see?’ He said: ‘Then the Jews shall swear.’ They said: ‘O Messenger of Allah, who would believe the Jews?’ He said: ‘Then I shall pay for your companion.’”

So I said to him: how is the ruling in it? He said: “Indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has ruled concerning bloodshed in a way that He has not ruled in anything from the rights of people, due to His magnifying blood. If a man claimed against another man ten thousand dirhams, less than that or more, the oath would not be upon the claimant; rather, the oath would be upon the one claimed against. But when a man claims blood against a people, alleging that they killed, then the oath is upon the claimant of blood before those claimed against. The claimant must bring fifty who swear that so-and-so killed so-and-so, then the one against whom the oath was sworn is delivered to them. If they wish, they pardon him; if they wish, they kill; and if they wish, they accept the blood money. If they do not swear, then those claimed against must have fifty men among them swear: ‘We did not kill him, nor did we know a killer for him.’ If they do that, the people of the village in which he was found must pay his blood money. And if he was in open land, his blood money is paid from the Bayt al-Mal. For Amir al-Mu’minin عليه السلام used to say: ‘The blood of a Muslim man is not to be left wasted.’”

key_terms.الدِّمَاءِ: cases of bloodshed and unlawful killing
key_terms.الدِّيَةَ: blood money paid in compensation for a killing
key_terms.الْقَسَامَةِ: the collective oath procedure used in homicide cases
key_terms.الْيَمِينُ: the legal oath used in adjudication
key_terms.بَيْتِ الْمَالِ: the public treasury from which liability may be paid
key_terms.فَتْحِ خَيْبَرَ: the conquest of Khaybar, the historical setting of the incident

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling of al-qasamah in murder cases, and how did it originate in Islamic law?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the origin and legal procedure of al-qasamah in murder cases, tracing it back to the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله after Khaybar. It highlights the special gravity of bloodshed in Islamic law, detailing how oaths, liability, blood money, and public responsibility are handled so that the blood of a Muslim is not left unavenged or neglected.
